hinge.question: that a garden is kept at all
hinge.end: that the beds feed the house through the year
hinge.method: read at each season: what each bed gave, counted and never judged

definitions.body: A plot kept for one crop at a time. It is turned between crops.

theses.title: The garden feeds the house.
theses.text: The garden is kept to feed the house. Each bed is planted for what the kitchen will use. What the house cannot use is given away.

terms.title: How it is said
anchors: The garden is kept to feed the house.

terms.title: Each bed
anchors: Each bed is planted for what the kitchen will use.

traditions.note: The almanac plants by the season.

questions.question: How is the garden's record worded?

theses.title: The record names the gardener plainly.
theses.text: The one the record is kept for is named the user. A word is fixed in its glossary entry and nowhere else.

questions.question: What is planted in a bed?

theses.title: A bed takes what the kitchen asks for.
theses.text: A bed takes the crop the kitchen asks for this season. A bed left empty is turned and rested. The rotation is written down before the seed goes in.

terms.title: The rotation
anchors: The rotation is written down before the seed goes in.

definitions.body: A bed rested for a season with nothing sown.

theses.title: The rotation is kept on one sheet.
theses.text: The rotation is kept on one sheet by the shed door. Every bed has a line on it. A fallow bed is marked with a cross.

questions.question: What does the almanac say of planting?

theses.title: Plant by the moon and the frost.
theses.text: The almanac plants after the last frost. It reads the moon for root crops.
